dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Hi there, Lorraine. Dennis Flynn here. Um, I've got a recycling question, if that's something you folks handle. Or maybe it's somebody else. I never know.
No, that's us. Go ahead, Dennis. What's the question?

Okay, so I'm standing here in my kitchen looking at a pizza box, and I'm thinking, does this go in the blue bin or not? Because I've been putting them in for a year and now I'm wondering if I've been doing it wrong the whole time. [pause] Ha. Which would be about me.
Well, let's sort it out. Is the box greasy, or is it pretty clean?
Oh, it's greasy. It's a Wednesday, I mean, it's last night's. Greasy, with a little cheese stuck on the lid. Yeah.

Okay. In general, the greasy or food-soiled part of a pizza box doesn't belong in recycling, because the oil ruins the paper. If the top is clean you can tear that off and recycle it, and the dirty bottom goes in with your regular trash.
Tear the top off. Clean top in the blue, dirty bottom in the trash. Got it. Hold on, let me write that, I've got a pen somewhere. [pause] Nope. Got it in my head. Ha.
That's fine. I'll say it again if you need it.

No, no, I've got it. Okay, second thing. Glass. Is glass still okay? Jars, bottles, that kind of thing? Because somebody told me they stopped taking glass and I thought, well, that can't be right, but then I thought, what do I know?

Glass bottles and jars are still accepted in the recycling. Just empty them and give them a quick rinse. Lids are fine to put back on. What we don't want is broken window glass, drinking glasses, or mirrors. Those are different from bottles and jars.

Oh, see, now that's a good one, because I did have a drinking glass that broke last week, and I think I put it in the blue bin. Oops. [pause] Ha. Well, now I know. Next time it goes in the trash, wrapped up so nobody gets cut.
Yes, wrap it in newspaper or put it in a box so the collectors don't get hurt.

Right, right. I should say, I'm a mail carrier myself, so I think about the guys on the trucks. I'm on my lunch break right now, actually, sitting down for ten minutes, so I figured I'd make the call before I forgot. Which I do, forget. Ha.
Well, good use of the lunch break. Anything else on your list?

Yes. Okay, the clamshells. You know, the clear plastic ones, the berries come in, or the salad, or the takeout containers. The hinged kind. Do those go in? Because they've got the little number on the bottom and I never know what the number means.
Those can be tricky. Can you read me the number on the bottom of one?
Let me look. I've got one from strawberries right here. [pause] Okay, it's a... it's a one? In the little triangle. Or maybe it's a seven. It's worn. Ha, I need my glasses.

That's okay. Generally, the clear clamshell containers are accepted in the recycling if they're clean and empty. I'd say rinse them out. If one is a number you can't read, I'd still put it in as long as it's clean and it's a hard plastic container. Anything greasy or full of food residue goes in the trash.
Clean and empty, hard plastic, in the blue. Okay. And what about the black ones? The black takeout trays?
Those are a problem, because the sorting equipment can't see black plastic well. Best to put those in the trash.

Black ones to the trash. Okay. I'm learning a lot here. [pause] Now, what was I going to ask next? Hang on. It was right there. Ha. Oh, a fee! Is there a fee? For any of this? Because I rent, and I don't get the bills for much, but I want to know if the city charges extra for recycling or for the bin.

As far as the curbside recycling goes, there's no separate charge to you for putting out the blue bin. It's part of the regular city service. If you ever needed a replacement bin there might be something different, and I can have somebody check on that if you ever get to that point.
No, my bin is fine. It's a little cracked on the handle but it works. No fee, that's what I wanted. My landlord will be thrilled. Ha.
Good. Now, can I have your address, just so I have it noted with the question, and I can tell you which pickup day you're on?
Sure, it's 356 Narragansett Avenue. Over in the Fifth Ward.
Three fifty-six Narragansett Avenue. Let me pull that up. [pause] Okay. Is that a single house or a multi-unit?
It's a house, I'm on the first floor, I mean the whole place is divided up, there's two of us. Me and the upstairs neighbor. But the bins are out front for both of us. Shared. We share. Ha.
Okay. And I'm showing your trash and recycling pickup on Thursday for that street. Does that sound right to you?
Thursday. Yes. That's, well, that's tomorrow. I thought it was Friday. Ha. See? That's why I called. I'd have put the bins out a day late.

Well, it's good you called. Tomorrow's Thursday, so tonight's the night to bring them to the curb. And recycling and trash go out the same day there, but I'd double check the calendar, because recycling can switch to every other week depending on the schedule.
Every other week? Oh no. Okay, so how do I know if it's this week or next week? Is there a calendar? Do you mail it?
There's a collection calendar on the city website, and I can look at it from here. Give me a moment. [pause] All right, I'm showing recycling is a pickup week tomorrow for your address.
Great. So out tonight, both bins. Okay. When I get home from work, about four-thirty or so, I'll haul them out. Before I forget. Ha.
That works. Just have them out by the morning, and keep them a few feet apart if you can, so the truck can get at each one.

A few feet apart. Okay. So let me say it back. Clean top of the pizza box in the blue, greasy bottom in the trash. Glass jars and bottles yes, but not drinking glasses or window glass. Clamshells yes if they're clean and hard plastic, black trays no. And no fee. Did I get all that?
You got it all. That's exactly right.
I'm proud of myself. Ha. Probably I'll forget the half of it by dinner, but I'll stick a note on the fridge.
And if you want, call back anytime and we'll go through it again.
I might. Thanks, Lorraine. Really. You were very patient with me. Oh, wait, do you need my phone number for the notes?
If you'd like to leave it, I can put it on the record.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-seven-four. Got it.
Perfect. Okay, my ten minutes are about up, the sorting room is going to wonder where I am. Thanks again.
You're welcome, Dennis. Enjoy the rest of your afternoon, and good luck with the route.
You too. Bye now.
